summary: ```markdown # CLO Master Direct Course Lesson 14: Wedding Dress Master Teaching Live Stream ## Introduction Hello, everyone. I'm Evelyn, a 3D designer and trainer from CLO, Shanghai. Today is my first time meeting you in the studio. Today's live stream is about wedding dresses, which are divided into two parts. In the upper part, I will show you how to make a wedding dress, involving different production points. I hope you can learn new knowledge by watching this live stream. Since there are many simulation parts in this live stream, I will show you how to record the video in advance. Let's start the live stream! ## Software Overview First of all, let's take a look at the software version of CLO 6.1. As you can see, many of our tools are hidden. To make it easier for us to create, let's go to the settings, click on the username, and then click on the user interface. We will change the position of the toolbar to the left and right and then turn off the tool selection. Now you can see that most of our tools are displayed. The virtual model used in this live stream is adjusted by Grace in our library. CLO 6.1 also has a new function that allows the model to wear makeup and adjust skin color. You can look forward to the live stream of CLO 6.1. ## Production Logic When we make a wedding dress, our production logic is very important. For large and multi-layer complex structure clothing, we must create it from the top to the bottom, starting from the internal support structure to the outer layer, layer by layer. Each time we start the creation and production of a new layer, we must ensure that the previous layer of production and simulation is in a stable state before proceeding to the next step. ### Creating the Top First, we can start to make the top. This step can be understood as making money in 3D. The tool used is our 3D pen virtual model. We can enter a number here. Let's begin by drawing the internal support structure of the dress. After drawing, we can add 3D segmentation lines to distinguish different pattern pieces. Once completed, we will use the Flatten tool to flatten the 3D line we just drew into a 2D version. After creating the version, make sure to arrange them in the 2D window to avoid confusion in the next production. I have deleted the previous line, and now I am going to edit the version and the sewing line. At the same time, we need to clone the version. Next, we need to check the version to make sure that the version we created is the same length as the one we created. Here, I have used the Flatten tool to adjust the position of the flange to ensure that it is the same length. Make sure there is not much difference between the lengths of the flanges. We will use the rectangle tool to ensure that the width of the flange is 1 cm and the height is the length of the sewing line. ### Sewing the Flange After we are done, we will make sure that the flange is placed on the other side of the flange. Next, we will freeze the flange and then sew it together. We need to ensure that the flange is displayed correctly in the 3D window. To sew the flange and the UI version together, we need to use the internal sewing line. Choose the two sides of the flange and add a 5 mm internal sewing line. After finishing, we can quickly sew it together and arrange it by adding it to the outside for more firmness and support. ### Setting Physical Attributes Note that in CLO, the meaning of the name is English or Pinyin. The name of the fabric is called "Cloth." I temporarily set our physical attribute to "Trim Hardware." After learning how to make an unchangeable physical attribute, we can go back and use the defined physical attribute fabric to modify and replace it. Put our fabric on our fishbone structure. We used the default fabric on number 1, so it's a bit loose. The top and bottom lines are usually supported by the fishbone. Therefore, we choose the top and bottom panel lines and add a sticky strip to support this part of the structure. After completion, we can modify it and freeze it. ## Building the Upper Body Now, let's move on to the next part of production. Since we started from the beginning, there is no conflict between the upper body and the lower body in the process of making our clothes. Therefore, we will start to make the upper body of the dress. First, I come to the window of my 2D version. In the menu, I display the texture surface of my 2D version window and change it to the display method of "Translucent Surface." We can connect our number 1 version through a point-to-connection point. Next, we use our original measurement clothing tool to determine the position of our line. Then, we use our editorial measurement clothing tool to hook it as an internal line. After we determine the position of our line, we use the rectangular plate tool to freely draw a rectangular plate on top of the plate and adjust its position. ### Rearranging Panels We will do the same logic on the display of the 2D version window, such as "Translucent Surface." You can select information talking with you from the window of this 2D version and hook it to the burrow. Next, through the point-to-connection point, we choose our internal multidirectional line tool to draw it out for the back panel. After we are done, we will rearrange the panels in the 2D window. We can add more panels if we want. Once we connect the points to form a closed point, we will cut it off. Now we use the same method on the back to build a closed line. During this process, I can add some volume to it and adjust its position. After we have a closed internal shape, we can check for any new points and cut them off if necessary. ### Sewing the Upper Body Next, we will quickly sew up the upper body using our 1 to n free sewing tool to put our outer layer and inner layer together. Pay attention to the place where we fold the sewing; we need to change the type of sewing thread to "Turned." After sewing, we will open the arrangement and simulate it. To prevent accidents in the following operations, I will save my project file first. Then we can start the production of the lower half of our clothes. ## Production of the Lower Half According to the previous production logic, we will start the production of the lower half of our clothes. The production of the clothes will involve creating the name of our wedding dress, which is something many of our friends are looking forward to. ### Two Methods for Creating the Dress There are actually many different ways to create the wedding dress. Due to time constraints, I will talk about two different methods. Each method has its own strengths and weaknesses. The first method is a more straightforward approach, while the second method involves adjusting the physical properties of the fabric to ensure that our skirt can withstand the outer layer's repeated structure. #### First Method For the first method, we need to arrange the waist belt at the point of arrangement of the waist. As you can see, our group name is relatively large, and the number of pieces is relatively large. Therefore, it is unrealistic to arrange it at the point of arrangement of the legs as usual. We need to use our positioning ball tool to arrange it in a state of closed simulation. I am using the positioning ball of the screen coordinate, so I switch to the right angles, such as front, back, side, and top to arrange it. #### Second Method The second method is to adjust the physical properties of the fabric so that our skirt will really become stiff, allowing it to withstand the repeated structure of the outer layer. This method is more demanding and requires a thorough understanding of our physical properties. First, create the fabric that we need to use and name it. Next, let's go to our property editor and click on the physical properties. We can see the strength of our silk thread and the tension of our corner line, which controls the stretch of our fabric. We will skip this for now and look at the bending strength. The bending strength controls the hardness of our fabric. The larger the value, the harder it is to bend. Now let's adjust the strength to the maximum. The bending strength is a percentage that determines how easily the fabric bends. We will set this value carefully based on our desired effect. ### Final Adjustments After creating the outer layer of the wedding dress, we can apply suitable fabrics in different parts of our wedding dress. In the window of my dummy room, I searched for silk and added three types of fabrics that we need. The main body of our wedding dress is usually made from this kind of fabric. As for the outer fabric, I want it to have a certain width, so I added organza fabric. For the upper body of our wedding dress, we need a thin fabric with a wide width, so we used a silk ribbon. ### Conclusion This live stream wraps up the first half of our wedding dress production. We discussed the structure of the wedding dress, and in the next half, we will delve into details like headscarves, flash diamonds, and various stickers. I hope you enjoyed this live stream and learned something new. If you have any questions, feel free to post them. Thank you for joining, and I look forward to seeing you in the next session! ```
